title: 3.4.10 Lab: Implicit-Return Rewrite Drill
description: Write three one-line arrow functions using implicit return, and call each one. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write three one-line arrows
steps.instructions: Create three const variables, each assigned a single-expression arrow function with no braces and no return keyword. Give each one a different job: for example, one that multiplies, one that answers a yes/no question, and one that joins two strings.

steps.title: Use implicit return
steps.instructions: Every arrow body must be a bare expression right after the `=>`. If you add braces, the implicit return stops working, so leave them off.

steps.title: Call each and log the results
steps.instructions: Call each of the three functions with sample arguments and print each result with console.log.

requirements.title: At least three arrow functions
requirements.description: Code contains three or more arrow functions. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Write three separate const variables, each holding its own arrow function, so the file has three arrows in all.

requirements.title: Implicit return used
requirements.description: Every arrow body is a bare expression: no arrow body starts with a brace. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Put the expression right after =>, with no braces. The value of that one expression is what the arrow hands back.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: Three named arrows, each called
requirements.description: Three different const names each hold an arrow with at least one parameter, and each one is called. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Give each arrow its own const name and at least one parameter, then call each one by its name: console.log(triple(4)).

requirements.title: all three results are printed
requirements.description: At least three values are printed. Help: 3.4.8 (Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Call each of the three arrows and print every result. Printing the three results on one line, separated by commas, is fine.

checks.fail: Print the result of each of your three arrows (one console.log each, or all three in one).

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.4.10 Lab: Implicit-Return Rewrite Drill". The task they were given: Create three const variables, each assigned a single-expression arrow function with no braces and no return keyword. Give each one a different job: for example, one that multiplies, one that answers a yes/no question, and one that joins two strings. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
